newsitem.title: EU: OUTCOME OF EU-TURKEY JOINT CONSULTATIVE COMMITTEE.
newsitem.headline: OUTCOME OF EU-TURKEY JOINT CONSULTATIVE COMMITTEE.

text.p: ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL COMMITTEE (ECOSOC) PRESS RELEASE
DOCUMENT DATE: JUNE 17, 1997
4th Meeting of the EU Turkey Joint Consultative Committee -
Gaziantep June 12, 1997 - Statement by the two co-chairmen

The EU Turkey Joint Consultative Committee made up of eighteen representatives of Turkish economic and social interest groups and an equal number of members of the Economic and Social Committee (ESC) of the European Conununities held its fourth meeting in Gaziantep on June 12, 1997 under the joint chairmanship of Mr Husamettin Kavi, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Istanbul Chamber of Industry and Mr Roger Briesch, Chairman of the ESC Workers Group.

The Committee examined the working of the EU-Turkey customs union with presentations by Mr Lake, head of the delegation of the European Commission M Ankara, Mr Kuneralp, Deputy Director General Turkish Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Mr Kudatgobilik. The Committee was pleased with the good results achieved in this area. It noted that the figures and the composition of the EU-Turkey bilateral trade balance following the implementation of the Customs Union should be examined cautiously and expressed its intention to pay special attention to the economic and social consequences of the customs union in the near future.

The Consultative Committee noted also that financial Cooperation has still not been put into effect 18 months after the implementation of the Customs union. It hoped that all the prerequisites would be met so that an appropriate solution could be found speedily. The Committee confirmed that this would also stimulate and increase in the flow of foreign direct investment to Turkey.

The Committee discussed the question of the Euromed Partnership with a presentation by Mrs Cassina from the ESC. Considering that the Economic and Social Committee of the EC has been asked by the Council to play an important role in the implementation of the Euromed Partnership and that the multilateral aspects and the bilateral dimensions of this Euromed Partnership are complementary, it was decided to improve the circulation of infomiation and to develop opportunities for exchanges and dialogue, in this context the creation of a network of economic and social partners of all the Mediterranean countries was discussed.

A presentation on the ESC policy towards Eastern and Central Europe prepared by Mr Gauder from ESC was given to the Committee. The Committee has noted with satisfaction the declaration of the President of Council that Turkey will be treated on the same criteria than other candidate countries. This question will be debated in depth at the next JCC meeting taking into consideration the Copenhagen criteria.
The Committee adopted a resolution on the energy sector within the framework of the relations between the European Union and Turkey. The rapporteurs were Mr Onen and Mr Beale.
The main proposals were the following:
. considering the low efficiency and serious environmental effects of lignite fire power plants and the need to use low quality lignite to meet its electricity has to develop a clean coal programme,
.a programme should be developed to decrease the losses in the electricity network,

.during the construction of nuclear power plants, Turkey has to develop a nuclear programme in order to meet the needs of qualified personnel, licensing, testing and standardisation, quality management and related infrastructure,
.Turkey has to take some precautions in order to diminish its import dependency on petroleum and natural gas,

.privatisation should not be the reason for the deformation of public sector and delays in energy sector investments. Prior to privatisation, constitutional, legal, contractual, pricing problems should be solved and precautions should be taken to protect consumer rights and to increase efficiency in the energy sector,
.considering the increasing demand for natural gas, import and consumption planning will be the main problem area,
.in order to keep energy imports at a controlable level, Turkey has to be more active in applications of renewable energy sources and improvement in energy efficiency.
The following fields were identified for useful co-operation:
.joint research and development programme on
-clean coal technologies for low quality Turkish lignite
-biotechnological processes in the energy sector
.improvement of "energy management" in industry (training activities for energy management as well as Environmental Impact Assessment and Environmental Management)
.data improvement for solar energy and wind energy potential in Turkey
.programme on energy forestry
.financial support for environmentally sound energy projects
.communication network for the exchange of data in the energy field with the participation of non governmental organisations.
The Committee also adopted a resolution on industrial SMEs vocational training. The rapporteurs were Mr Yorganci and Mr Pezzini.

.Having regard to the statement by the President of the Council of the European Union at the 38th meeting of the EU-Turkey Association Council 29 April 1997 on the implementation of the joint resolution adopted on 6 March 1995, reiterating that the Council was "ready to start a dialogue on the possible participation of Turkey in the community programmes planned in the fields of co-operation covered by that resolution" and

.Considering that in a context of far reaching integration such as a customs union, Turkey could not be excluded from programmes which are already accessible to the EFTA countries, the CEEC's, Cyprus and Malta.
The Committee:
.called upon the European Commission to present a proposal to amend Council Decision 97/15/EC on the 1997-2000 multi-annual Programme so as to include Turkey among the beneficiary countries

.called upon the EU-Turkey association bodies to define by common accord the arrangements for cooperation in fields affecting SMEs, particularly with a view to harmonising existing national measures in Turkey with Community priorities
.suggested the setting up of specialised working groups to include experts from bodies representing both European and Turkish SMEs, particularly in the areas of common interest

.stressed the importance of upgrading statistical data and methods as regards SMEs, and the need to harmonise them, in particular by including Turkey in the annual reports of the European Observatory for SMEs. In the same context, the Committee calls upon the Turkish authorities to harmonise definitions relating to SMEs and craft industries with those used in the EU countries.
As regards vocational training, the Committee took the view that:

.it was essential for Turkey to be included in the Leonardo, Socrates and Youth for Europe programmes in time for the 1998 projects. The Joint Committee therefore calls upon the European Parliament and the Council to ensure the rapid adoption of this Commission proposal

.the present Turkish Government's plan to extend compulsory schooling to a total of eight years by combining the primary and lower secondary stages is of the highest importance. To that end the Committee asked the authorities to put this reform into practice as planned at the start of the next school year

.EU-Turkey co-operation in the field of technical and vocational training offered considerable potential for job creation and hence for reducing the pressure from migratory flows, both internal and external. This co-operation will also provide an opportunity to harmonise the certification of vocational qualifications and define vocational standards and requirements for access to professions

.the Turkish Government should reallocate the Fund for Development and Extension of Technical, Vocational and Apprenticeship Training, which was transferred to the general budget following the economic crisis of April 1994

.the overall budget devoted to education in Turkey (2,4 % of GNP) is well below the European average. It draws the attention of the Turkish authorities to the need to allocate additional resources both to additional education and to technical and vocational education.

The Committee was pleased to note the models of successful co-operation in Turkey between the public and private sectors, involving local representative bodies, and European partners. However it felt that it was essential to ensure the effective, direct involvement of all the social-economic players, including employers and workers in industry, commerce and services including tourism.

Broadening the range of sectors covered by apprenticeship and vocational training was also considered as a measure of importance for the economic and social emancipation of young women in Turkey. To that end the Committee hoped that the inclusion of Turkey in the Leonardo programme will lead to judicious development of the human resources represented by young Turkish women.

The Committee suggested that trilateral co-operation with the EU be developed in vocational training, and to that end calls upon the EU-Turkey Association Council to look the arrangements for Turkey's active participation in the work of the European training foundation in Turin.
